newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: SOCCER-BRITISH EXPERTS IDENTIFY CAUSES OF STADIUM TRAGEDY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRITISH EXPERTS IDENTIFY CAUSES OF STADIUM TRAGEDY.

text.p: British experts in stadium safety say a combination of inadequate spectator control, poor security and stadium design flaws caused the disaster at Guatemala's national soccer arena which claimed 81 lives.
The two experts, an architect and a stadium safety management consultant, said late on Friday they had made a series of recommendations about crowd control improvements to the government.

The Britons prepared a report on security recommendations for the government after spending this week in Guatemala researching the factors that contributed to the deadly crush of fans October 16. The report has not yet been made public.
"A lot of the recommendations we will make are about attitudes toward security," James Chalmer, security expert with the British Football Licencing Authority, told a news conference.
He said no single factor, but a combination of factors including lack of spectator control, stadium design and security systems, probably caused the disaster.
Regulatory measures to control the flow of spectators into the stadium, and monitoring the number of people in different parts of the stadium, are among the pair's recommendations.

The tragedy in the cheap seats on cement terraces at one end of Guatemala's Mateo Flores stadium happened half an hour before kick-off at a World Cup qualifying match between Guatemala and Costa Rica.
No matches have been played there since, and Guatemala was this week ordered by FIFA, soccer's world governing body, to play its home World Cup qualifying matches at neutral fields.
The experts will also recommend procedures to determine the safe capacity of stadiums, which several investigating teams in Guatemala have been working to establish.

State prosecutors oversaw a count of tickets taken on the night of the tragedy which established the stadium was probably not crowded beyond its historic capacity, which different sports authorities have measured between 45,000 and 48,000.
But new measurements of seating areas, aisles, and safety exits have established the true stadium capacity may be closer to 32,000.
